title: Toy Joy: 3D Shapes and Nets
seo_title: 3D Shapes and Nets Class 3 Worksheet with Answers (Maths Mela Chapter 2)
standard_code: Class 3, Maths Mela Chapter 2: Toy Joy
standard_text: 3D shapes: identifying cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones and spheres in toys; faces, edges and corners; nets of a cube and cuboid (summary of NCERT Maths Mela Class 3)
meta_desc: Class 3 Toy Joy worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 2): cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones and spheres, faces, edges, corners and nets. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Faces, edges and corners describe a solid.
key_sub: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A face is a flat surface, an edge is where two faces meet, a corner (vertex) is where edges meet.
  • A net is the flat shape that folds into a solid.

Examples

Example

How many faces does a cuboid have?

Top, bottom, front, back, left, right

Answer: 6

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting only the faces you can seeRemember the hidden faces at the back and bottom.
Calling a cube a squareA square is flat; a cube is solid.

faq.a: A flat pattern that can be folded to make a solid shape.

faq.q: How many corners does a cube have?

items.q: What is the name of this object?
items.e: It has 6 faces and they are all squares of the same size, so it is a cube.

items.q: Name this 3D object.
items.e: It has 6 faces and they are all squares of the same size, so it is a cube. It is turned, but it is still a cube.

items.q: What is this object called?
items.e: It has 6 rectangle faces and they are not all squares, so it is a cuboid.

items.q: What is the name of this object?
items.e: It has 6 rectangle faces and they are not all squares, so it is a cuboid. It is standing on its end, but it is still a cuboid.

items.q: Name this 3D object.
items.e: It has 6 rectangle faces and they are not all squares, so it is a cuboid. It is turned, but it is still a cuboid.

items.q: What is this object called?
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. It does not come to a point, so it is not a pyramid.

items.q: What is the name of this object?
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. It does not come to a point, so it is not a pyramid. It is standing on a triangle face, but it is still a triangular prism.

items.q: Name this 3D object.
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. It does not come to a point, so it is not a pyramid. It is turned so you see a triangle end at the front.

items.q: What is this object called?
items.e: It has a square face at the bottom and 4 triangle faces that meet at a point, so it is a square-based pyramid.

items.q: What is the name of this object?
items.e: It has a square face at the bottom and 4 triangle faces that meet at a point, so it is a square-based pyramid. It is turned, but it is still a square-based pyramid.

items.q: Name this 3D object.
items.e: It has a triangle at the bottom and 3 triangle faces that meet at a point, so it is a triangle-based pyramid.
It has 2 flat circle faces at the ends and a curved surface, so it is a cylinder. A circle is only a flat 2D shape.
It has 2 flat circle faces at the ends and a curved surface, so it is a cylinder. A circle is only a flat 2D shape. It is lying on its side, but it is still a cylinder.
It has 1 flat circle face and a curved surface that comes to a point, so it is a cone.
It has 1 flat circle face and a curved surface that comes to a point, so it is a cone. It is upside down, but it is still a cone.
It is round all over, like a ball, so it is a sphere. A circle is a flat 2D shape.

items.q: Both pictures show the same object in different positions. What is it?
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. It does not come to a point, so it is not a pyramid. Turning an object does not change its name.
B is a cone: it has 1 circle face and comes to a point. It is lying on its side.

items.q: Which picture shows a square-based pyramid?
items.e: D is a square-based pyramid: it has a square base and 4 triangles that meet at a point. A triangular prism has no point, and a triangle-based pyramid has a triangle base.
C is a cylinder: it has 2 circle faces and a curved surface. It is lying on its side.

items.q: A flat surface of a 3D object is called a …
items.e: A face is a flat surface. An edge is where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner.

items.q: The line where two faces of an object meet is called an …
items.e: Where two faces meet there is an edge.

items.q: A corner of an object, where edges meet, is called a …
items.e: A corner is a vertex. More than one vertex are called vertices.

items.q: This is a cube. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: This is a cube. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This is a cube. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too.

items.q: This is a cuboid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: This is a cuboid. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A cuboid has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. Some faces are at the back or underneath. You cannot see them, but you must count them too.

items.q: A flat surface of a 3-D shape is called a …
items.e: A face is a flat surface. An edge is where two faces meet. A vertex is a corner.

items.q: The line where two faces of a 3-D shape meet is called an …
items.e: Where two faces meet there is an edge.

items.q: A corner of a 3-D shape, where edges meet, is called a …
items.e: A corner is a vertex. More than one vertex are called vertices.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. The dashed lines show edges at the back. Count them too.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces, 8 edges and 5 vertices. Some vertices are at the back, where the dashed lines meet. Count them too. Do not forget the vertex at the top.

items.q: How many vertices does a cuboid have?
items.e: A cuboid has 8 vertices: 4 at the top and 4 at the bottom. 12 is the number of edges.

items.q: Which 3-D shape has 5 vertices?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 4 vertices round the square and 1 at the top: 4 + 1 = 5.

items.q: Which 3-D shape has no flat faces, no edges and no vertices?
items.e: A sphere is round all over, like a ball. It has only one curved surface.

items.q: A net is a flat shape that you can fold to make a 3D object. How many squares are in a net of a cube?
items.e: A cube has 6 faces, so its net has 6 squares. 8 is the number of vertices and 12 is the number of edges.

items.q: Which net folds into a cube?
items.e: A has 6 squares and each one folds onto a different face. B: it has only 5 squares, so one face is missing; C: two squares are on the same side of the row of 4, so they fold onto the same face; D: it has a 2 by 2 block of squares, so two squares overlap.

items.q: Which net folds into a cube?
items.e: B has 6 squares and each one folds onto a different face. A: 5 squares in a row wrap all the way around, so two squares overlap; C: it has 7 squares, but a cube has only 6 faces; D: two squares are on the same side of the row of 4, so they fold onto the same face.

items.q: Which net folds into a cube?
items.e: C has 6 squares and each one folds onto a different face. A: it has a 2 by 2 block of squares, so two squares overlap; B: two squares are on the same side of the row of 4, so they fold onto the same face; D: it has only 5 squares, so one face is missing.

items.q: Which net folds into a cube?
items.e: D has 6 squares and each one folds onto a different face. A: two squares are on the same side of the row of 4, so they fold onto the same face; B: 5 squares in a row wrap all the way around, so two squares overlap; C: it has 7 squares, but a cube has only 6 faces.

items.q: Which net will NOT fold into a cube?
items.e: C will not work: two squares are on the same side of the row of 4, so they fold onto the same face. The other three nets each make a cube.

items.q: Which net will NOT fold into a cube?
items.e: A will not work: it has a 2 by 2 block of squares, so two squares overlap. The other three nets each make a cube.

items.q: Will this net fold into a cube?
c: No: only a cross shape makes a cube.
No: the squares are not in a straight line.
No: a cube net needs 8 squares.
Yes: each square folds onto a different face.
items.e: It has 6 squares and none of them overlap when you fold it. There are 11 different nets of a cube, not only the cross.

items.q: Will this net fold into a cube?
c: No: a cube net needs 8 squares.
No: two squares fold onto the same face.
Yes: it has a row of 4 squares.
items.e: The 2 squares on top of the row of 4 both fold up onto the top face. The bottom face is left open. Having 6 squares is not enough.

items.q: What happens when you fold this net?
c: It makes a box with one face missing.
items.e: The net has only 5 squares. A cube has 6 faces, so one face is left open, like a box with no lid.

items.q: Which 3D object does this net make?
items.e: It has 6 faces: 4 rectangles and 2 squares. The faces are not all squares, so it folds into a cuboid, not a cube.

items.q: Which 3D object does this net make?
items.e: It has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles. The triangles become the ends, so it is a triangular prism. A pyramid net has triangles that meet at a point.

items.q: Which 3D object does this net make?
items.e: It has 1 square and 4 triangles. The square is the base and the 4 triangles fold up to meet at a point: a square-based pyramid.

items.q: Which 3D object does this net make?
items.e: It has 4 triangles. One is the base and the other 3 fold up to meet at a point: a triangle-based pyramid.

items.q: Which net folds into a triangular prism?
items.e: D: it has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles. The others: A makes a square-based pyramid, B makes a cube, C makes a cuboid.

items.q: Which net folds into a square-based pyramid?
items.e: B: it has 1 square and 4 triangles that meet at a point. The others: A makes a cuboid, C makes a cube, D makes a triangular prism.

items.q: How many triangles are in the net of a square-based pyramid?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 1 square and 4 triangles. The net has the same faces: 4 triangles.

items.q: Which shapes do you need for the net of a triangular prism?
items.e: A net has the same faces as the object. A triangular prism has 2 triangle ends and 3 rectangles.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face A?
items.e: A and F are in the same line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite faces. Squares that touch in the net are next to each other on the cube.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face B?
items.e: B and D are in the same line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite faces. Squares that touch in the net are next to each other on the cube.

items.q: You build a skeleton of a 3D object with sticks and connectors. Each stick is …
items.e: A stick is a straight line between two corners, so each stick is an edge.

items.q: In a skeleton, each connector (like a ball of modelling clay) is …
items.e: The connectors join the sticks at the corners, so each connector is a vertex.

items.q: This is a skeleton of a cube. How many sticks does it have?
items.e: A cube has 12 edges, so the skeleton has 12 sticks. Count the lighter sticks at the back too.

items.q: This is a skeleton of a cube. How many connectors does it have?
items.e: A cube has 8 vertices, so the skeleton has 8 connectors. 12 is the number of sticks.

items.q: This is a skeleton of a cuboid. How many sticks does it have?
items.e: A cuboid has 12 edges, so the skeleton has 12 sticks. Count the lighter sticks at the back too.

items.q: This is a skeleton of a triangular prism. How many sticks does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 9 edges, so the skeleton has 9 sticks. Count the lighter sticks at the back too.

items.q: This is a skeleton of a triangular prism. How many connectors does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 6 vertices, so the skeleton has 6 connectors. 9 is the number of sticks.

items.q: This is a skeleton of a square-based pyramid. How many sticks does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 8 edges, so the skeleton has 8 sticks. Count the lighter sticks at the back too.

items.q: This is a skeleton of a triangle-based pyramid. How many sticks does it have?
items.e: A triangle-based pyramid has 6 edges, so the skeleton has 6 sticks. Count the lighter sticks at the back too.

items.q: This is a skeleton of a triangle-based pyramid. How many connectors does it have?
items.e: A triangle-based pyramid has 4 vertices, so the skeleton has 4 connectors. 6 is the number of sticks.

items.q: Which object is this skeleton?
items.e: It has 2 triangles at the ends joined by 3 sticks: 9 sticks and 6 connectors. It does not come to a point, so it is a prism.

items.q: Which object is this skeleton?
items.e: It has a square at the bottom and 4 sticks that meet at a point on top: 8 sticks and 5 connectors. It is a square-based pyramid.

items.q: What do you need to build a skeleton of a cube?
items.e: A cube has 12 edges (sticks) and 8 vertices (connectors). 6 is the number of faces.

items.q: What do you need to build a skeleton of a square-based pyramid?
items.e: Edges: 4 around the square and 4 up to the top = 8 sticks. Vertices: 4 around the square and 1 at the top = 5 connectors.

items.q: Priya uses 9 sticks and 6 connectors to build one skeleton. Which object is it?
items.e: 9 edges and 6 vertices: that is a triangular prism. A square-based pyramid has 8 edges and 5 vertices.

items.q: Sneha uses 6 sticks and 4 connectors to build one skeleton. Which object is it?
items.e: 6 edges and 4 vertices: that is a triangle-based pyramid. A square-based pyramid needs 8 sticks and 5 connectors.

items.q: Siddharth builds a skeleton of a cube. What must be true about the sticks?
c: They are all the same length.
items.e: All the faces of a cube are the same square, so all 12 edges are the same length.

items.q: Meera has 8 short sticks and 4 long sticks. She uses all 12 to build a skeleton. Which object is it?
items.e: 12 sticks make a box shape with 8 corners. The sticks are not all the same length, so it is a cuboid, not a cube.

items.q: Which object can you NOT build as a skeleton with straight sticks?
items.e: A sphere is curved all over. It has no straight edges and no vertices, so sticks cannot make it.

items.q: Aditya builds a triangle-based pyramid and a cube. How many sticks does he use altogether?
items.e: A triangle-based pyramid has 6 edges and a cube has 12. 6 + 12 = 18 sticks. 10 adds the faces (4 + 6) instead.

items.q: A can of soup is shaped like which 3D object?
items.e: A can has 2 circle ends and a curved side, so it is a cylinder.

items.q: An ice cream cone is shaped like which 3D object?
items.e: It has a circle at the top, a curved side and a point at the bottom, so it is a cone.

items.q: A box of crackers is shaped like which 3D object?
items.e: It has 6 rectangle faces that are not all squares, so it is a cuboid.

items.q: A football ball is shaped like which 3D object?
items.e: A football ball is round all over, so it is a sphere. A circle is flat.

items.q: A number cube (a die) is shaped like which 3D object?
items.e: It has 6 square faces that are all the same size, so it is a cube.

items.q: A tea bag is shaped like a pyramid with 4 triangle faces. Which 3D object is it?
items.e: 4 triangle faces: 1 triangle base and 3 triangles that meet at a point. That is a triangle-based pyramid.

items.q: A tissue box sits on Fatima’s desk. She can see 3 of its faces. How many faces can she NOT see?
items.e: A box (cuboid) has 6 faces. 6 − 3 = 3 faces are at the back and underneath.

items.q: Meera paints a box for a recycling project. She paints every face except the bottom. How many faces does she paint?
items.e: A box has 6 faces. All but the bottom: 6 − 1 = 5 faces. 3 is only the faces you see from the front.

items.q: Aarav puts one number cube on top of another to make a tower on the table. How many faces of the cubes touch the table or the other cube?
items.e: The bottom cube touches the table with 1 face. The two cubes touch each other with 1 face each: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.

items.q: Rahul glues a piece of ribbon along every edge of a cube-shaped gift box. How many pieces of ribbon does he need?
items.e: A cube has 12 edges, so Rahul needs 12 pieces. 8 is the number of vertices and 6 is the number of faces.

items.q: Nikhil makes 2 cube boxes from paper nets. How many paper squares are there in the 2 nets?
items.e: Each cube net has 6 squares. 6 + 6 = 12 squares. 16 counts the vertices (8 + 8) instead.

items.q: Manav’s class builds 3 cube skeletons for a display in the hallway. How many sticks do they use?
items.e: Each cube needs 12 sticks. 12 + 12 + 12 = 36 sticks. 24 uses the 8 vertices (8 × 3) instead.

items.q: What is the name of this 3-D shape?
items.e: It has 6 faces and they are all squares of the same size, so it is a cube.

items.q: Name this 3-D shape.
items.e: It has 6 faces and they are all squares of the same size, so it is a cube. It is turned, but it is still a cube.

items.q: What is this 3-D shape called?
items.e: It has 6 rectangle faces and they are not all squares, so it is a cuboid.

items.q: What is the name of this 3-D shape?
items.e: It has 6 rectangle faces and they are not all squares, so it is a cuboid. It is standing on its end, but it is still a cuboid.

items.q: Name this 3-D shape.
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. A pyramid comes to a point; a prism does not.

items.q: What is this 3-D shape called?
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. It is standing on a triangle face, but it is still a triangular prism. A pyramid comes to a point; a prism does not.

items.q: What is the name of this 3-D shape?
items.e: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends, joined by 3 rectangles, so it is a triangular prism. It is turned so you see a triangle end at the front. A pyramid comes to a point; a prism does not.

items.q: Name this 3-D shape.
items.e: It has a square face at the bottom and 4 triangle faces that meet at a point, so it is a square-based pyramid.
